claims.claim: The summons-content requirements apply except as otherwise required by statute.
claims.quote: (a) Except as otherwise required by statute, a summons shall be directed to the defendant, signed by the clerk and issued under the seal of the court in which the action is pending, and it shall contain:
claims.note: The qualification applies to the required notice.

claims.claim: The summons must warn that unless the defendant responds, default will be entered upon the plaintiff’s application.
claims.quote:
(3) A direction that the defendant file with the court a written pleading in response to the complaint within 30 days after summons is served on the defendant.
(4) A notice that, unless the defendant so responds, their default will be entered upon application by the plaintiff,
claims.note: The default consequence and application requirement are supported. “So responds” refers specifically to filing a written pleading with the court within 30 days after service.

claims.claim: The notice says the plaintiff may apply to the court for the relief demanded in the complaint.
claims.quote: the plaintiff may apply to the court for the relief demanded in the complaint
claims.note: Application for relief is distinct from its award.

claims.claim: Possible results include garnishment of wages, taking of money or property, or other relief.
claims.quote: which could result in garnishment of wages, taking of money or property, or other relief.
claims.note: Each is described as possible, not automatic.

claims.claim: Whether a general denial suffices depends on whether the complaint is verified.
claims.quote: If the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1 or is not verified, a general denial is sufficient but only puts in issue the material allegations of the complaint.
claims.note: Verification matters, but the draft omits the separate Article 2 condition. A general denial, when sufficient, puts only material allegations in issue.

claims.claim: Assignment of the claim to a third party for collection affects whether a general denial suffices.
claims.quote: However, if the cause of action is a claim assigned to a third party for collection and the complaint is verified, the denial of the allegations shall be made positively or according to the information and belief of the defendant, even if the complaint is subject to Article 2 (commencing with Section 90) of Chapter 5.1 of Title 1 of Part 1.
claims.note: The assignment rule requires both assignment and verification. When both are present, the specified form of denial is mandatory even under Article 2.

claims.claim: Section 85 requires all its conditions to be met for an action to be treated as a limited civil case.
claims.quote: an action or special proceeding shall be treated as a limited civil case only if all of the following conditions are satisfied:
claims.note: The draft does not treat the dollar limit as sufficient by itself.

claims.claim: One Section 85 condition is that the amount in controversy does not exceed $35,000.
claims.quote: (a) The amount in controversy does not exceed thirty-five thousand dollars ($35,000).

flags.text: “Responds” omits what must be filed, where, and by when: a written pleading with the court within 30 days after service.
Verification and assignment alone do not distinguish verified, unassigned complaints subject to Article 2 from those outside it. Section 85’s dollar limit does not resolve that question.
A reader could mistake an informal reply for the required filing and face default, or use a general denial where §431.30(d) requires denial positively or on information and belief.

result.summary: The possible consequences of default and the Section 85 claims are supported. The draft omits the filing requirement that gives “responds” its meaning and does not explain when Article 2 or the verified assigned-claim rule changes the required denial.
